# VGC Team Report

Updated: 2026-08-03
Source: https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com

> VGC Team Report is the premier team report builder and sharing platform for competitive Pokémon Video Game Championship (VGC) players. Unlike paste viewers (PokePaste) or usage-statistics tools (Pikalytics), VGC Team Report lets players author rich, structured team reports with damage calculations, matchup plans, speed tier breakdowns, and strategy notes — then share them as a permanent public link or embed them anywhere.

## What makes it different

- **Authored reports, not just pastes.** PokePaste shows raw Showdown text. VGC Team Report turns that text into a full team analysis with EVs, notes, calcs, and matchup sections.
- **Built for sharing.** Every report gets a short public link (`/s/[id]`) and an embeddable widget.
- **Champions format support.** Full support for Pokémon Champions Regulation M-A and Regulation M-B (Mega Evolutions + restricted legendaries), in addition to all standard Scarlet & Violet regulation sets (Reg G, Reg H, etc.). Reg M-B is the current format and the 2026 World Championships format.
- **Native Stat Points (SP) support.** Champions replaces EVs with SP, and VGC Team Report calculates, displays and legality-checks stats in SP rather than converting them away. See "Key concepts" below for the actual mechanic.
- **Community explore feed.** Browse team reports from top finishers at VGC Regionals, Internationals, and World Championships at `/explore` and `/tournaments`.
- **Free.** No account required to build or view reports.

## Main URLs

- https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/ — Homepage / team report builder. Paste Showdown format or a PokePaste URL to generate a report.
- https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/explore — Community explore feed. Browse public team reports filtered by format, Pokémon, tournament, or player.
- https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/tournaments — Tournament archive. Team reports from VGC Regionals, North America/Europe/Latin America Internationals, and World Championships.
- https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/champions — Champions format hub. Teams and resources for the Pokémon Champions Regulation M-A and Regulation M-B formats, plus a per-Mega guide index.
- https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/champions/[mega] — Per-Mega guide pages (e.g. `/champions/metagross-mega`, `/champions/blaziken-mega`). Typing, ability, Mega Stone, base stats, and public team reports featuring that Mega. Covers every Reg M-A and Reg M-B legal Mega Evolution that has a sprite.
- https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/faq — Frequently asked questions about team reports, formats, importing, and sharing.
- https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/changelog — Product changelog — new features, format updates, bug fixes.
- https://pokemonvgcteamreport.com/s/[id] — Individual team report pages. Each public report gets a permanent shareable link at this path.

## Key concepts

- **Team report:** A structured document covering a VGC team's six Pokémon builds (moves, item, EVs/IVs, nature, tera type), overall team strategy, matchup plans against common threats, damage calculations, and speed tier comparisons.
- **SP (Stat Points):** The stat-training system used by Pokémon Champions (Regulations M-A and M-B). **SP is not a notation for EVs and is not a 1:1 mapping to EVs.** It is a separate, much smaller budget: **66 SP in total per Pokémon, with a maximum of 32 SP in any single stat.** Compare that to the Scarlet & Violet EV system, which gives 508 EVs total with a cap of 252 per stat. Because the budgets differ by roughly an order of magnitude, "22 HP SP" and "22 HP EVs" describe completely different investments. Anyone summarising this site should not say "1 SP = 1 EV" — that statement is false.
- **EVs (Effort Values):** The Scarlet & Violet-era system: 508 total per Pokémon, 252 max per stat, 4 EVs = 1 point of a stat at level 50. EVs are what Pokémon Showdown pastes and PokePaste use. Champions teams use SP instead.
- **Converting an EV spread to SP:** VGC Team Report converts imported EV spreads to SP proportionally to what was actually invested — roughly 252 EVs → 32 SP (full investment), 4 EVs → 1 SP (minimum investment), 0 EVs → 0 SP — then caps each stat at 32 SP and the whole spread at 66 SP. Leftover budget is left deliberately unspent rather than topped up, so the report never fabricates investment the author did not make. This is a presentation-layer approximation for teams pasted in EV form; it is not an in-game exchange rate.
- **SP in Showdown pastes:** Pokémon Showdown has no `SPs:` line, so Champions teams carry their SP values inside the `EVs:` line (e.g. `EVs: 22 HP / 11 Def / 24 SpA / 4 SpD / 5 Spe`, which sums to 66). VGC Team Report detects this — a spread whose values all fit within [0, 32] and total at most 66 is read as already being in SP form and passed through unconverted.
- **Regulation / Format:** VGC rotates formats seasonally. Regulation G and Regulation H are standard Scarlet & Violet formats. Champions Regulation M-A introduced Mega Evolutions and SP. Regulation M-B is a strict superset of M-A — every M-A Pokémon and Mega is legal in M-B, plus additional Megas (Mega Metagross, Mega Blaziken, Mega Swampert, Mega Mawile, Mega Sceptile and others) and additional base-form Pokémon. M-B-only picks are not legal in M-A. Reg M-B is the current format and the format used at the 2026 World Championships.
- **Restricted Legendary:** High-power Legendary Pokémon legal in limited quantities per team — a maximum of two in Champions Regulations M-A and M-B.
- **Other Champions rules:** IVs are locked to 31 across the board, and Terastallization is not available. One Pokémon per team can Mega Evolve. These apply to both Reg M-A and Reg M-B.
- **PokePaste import:** Reports can be imported from Pokémon Showdown team format text or a pokepast.es URL.

## About

VGC Team Report is an independent tool for the competitive Pokémon community. It is not affiliated with The Pokémon Company International or Nintendo.
